external_entities.name: sensor node
external_entities.description: A deployed node installed on a customer site that publishes readings and polls for firmware updates.
external_entities.source_excerpt: a few thousand sensor nodes installed on customer sites
external_entities.notes: Nodes are outside the organisation's physical control.

external_entities.name: field technician
external_entities.description: A technician who services sensor nodes over a local serial console.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Field technicians service nodes over a local serial console.

external_entities.name: fleet operator
external_entities.description: An operator who views telemetry dashboards from the corporate network.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Our own fleet operators look at dashboards over BigQuery from the corporate network

processes.name: device gateway
processes.description: An MQTT broker running on GKE that accepts readings from sensor nodes and forwards them to Pub/Sub.
processes.source_excerpt: the device gateway, which is an MQTT broker we run on GKE

processes.name: telemetry normalizer
processes.description: A Python consumer in the analytics network that picks up readings from Pub/Sub and writes them into the telemetry lake.
processes.source_excerpt: the telemetry normalizer, a Python consumer in our analytics network

processes.name: dashboard
processes.description: A dashboard used by fleet operators to view telemetry over BigQuery.
processes.source_excerpt: fleet operators look at dashboards over BigQuery

data_stores.name: device registry
data_stores.description: A Firestore registry used to check node keys and identify the customer associated with a node.
data_stores.source_excerpt: a device registry (Firestore) to check the key and to find out which customer the node belongs to

data_stores.name: Pub/Sub
data_stores.description: A messaging service onto which accepted readings are forwarded for consumption by the telemetry normalizer.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Readings the gateway accepts are forwarded onto Pub/Sub

data_stores.name: telemetry lake
data_stores.description: A BigQuery data store containing site addresses and occupancy patterns from the sensor fleet.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The lake has site addresses and occupancy patterns in it, so it is customer data.

data_stores.name: Cloud Storage bucket
data_stores.description: A bucket from which sensor nodes poll for firmware images. It is publicly readable.
data_stores.source_excerpt: nodes poll a Cloud Storage bucket for a new image
data_stores.notes: The bucket is public read. The source does not state whether firmware images are signed.

data_flows.name: publish readings
data_flows.description: Sensor nodes publish readings to the device gateway.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Each node publishes readings over MQTT to the device gateway

data_flows.name: look up device
data_flows.description: The device gateway looks up a device in the device registry to check its key and identify its customer.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The gateway looks up the device in a device registry (Firestore) to check the key and to find out which customer the node belongs to.

data_flows.name: forward readings
data_flows.description: The device gateway forwards accepted readings onto Pub/Sub.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Readings the gateway accepts are forwarded onto Pub/Sub

data_flows.name: pick up readings
data_flows.description: The telemetry normalizer picks up readings from Pub/Sub.
data_flows.source_excerpt: picked up by the telemetry normalizer

data_flows.name: write readings
data_flows.description: The telemetry normalizer writes readings into the telemetry lake.
data_flows.source_excerpt: which writes them into the telemetry lake in BigQuery

data_flows.name: read image
data_flows.description: A sensor node polls the Cloud Storage bucket for a firmware image.
data_flows.source_excerpt: nodes poll a Cloud Storage bucket for a new image and install what they find

data_flows.name: service node
data_flows.description: A field technician services a sensor node over its local serial console.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Field technicians service nodes over a local serial console.
data_flows.notes: Authentication on the console is unknown: "I don't know what authentication that console has, if any."

data_flows.name: view dashboard
data_flows.description: A fleet operator views a dashboard from the corporate network.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Our own fleet operators look at dashboards over BigQuery from the corporate network

data_flows.name: query data
data_flows.description: The dashboard accesses telemetry data in BigQuery.

trust_boundaries.name: customer sites
trust_boundaries.description: Sites where sensor nodes are installed and where the organisation does not have physical control of the nodes.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: sensor nodes installed on customer sites
trust_boundaries.notes: The nodes are outside the organisation's physical control.

trust_boundaries.name: cloud services
trust_boundaries.description: The cloud-hosted services named in the description, including GKE, Firestore, Pub/Sub, BigQuery, and Cloud Storage.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: an MQTT broker we run on GKE

trust_boundaries.name: analytics network
trust_boundaries.description: The network containing the telemetry normalizer.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: a Python consumer in our analytics network

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network from which fleet operators access dashboards.

assumptions.assumption: The customer sites are a tenant trust zone because they are outside the organisation's physical control and are customer-controlled locations.
assumptions.basis: The description says sensor nodes are installed on customer sites and are outside the organisation's physical control.

assumptions.assumption: The named GKE, Firestore, Pub/Sub, BigQuery, and Cloud Storage components share a cloud-services tenant boundary.
assumptions.basis: The description identifies the components as GKE, Firestore, Pub/Sub, BigQuery, and Cloud Storage services operated in a cloud-hosted environment.

assumptions.assumption: The device gateway is in the cloud-services boundary because it runs on GKE.
assumptions.basis: The device gateway is described as an MQTT broker run on GKE.

assumptions.assumption: The device gateway is internet-facing because it is exposed to the internet for nodes dialing in from anywhere.
assumptions.basis: The description says the gateway is exposed to the internet because the nodes dial in from anywhere.

assumptions.assumption: The device gateway has a non-web interface because it is an MQTT broker.
assumptions.basis: The description identifies the device gateway as an MQTT broker.

assumptions.assumption: The telemetry normalizer is internal because it runs in the analytics network.
assumptions.basis: The description places the telemetry normalizer in the analytics network.

assumptions.assumption: The telemetry normalizer has a non-web interface because it is a Python consumer.
assumptions.basis: The description identifies it as a Python consumer rather than a web application.

assumptions.assumption: The device registry contains confidential data because it stores a pre-shared key and customer association information.
assumptions.basis: The registry is used to check the key and determine which customer a node belongs to.

assumptions.assumption: Pub/Sub carries confidential data because the gateway forwards accepted sensor readings onto it.
assumptions.basis: The readings forwarded to Pub/Sub are the same accepted readings later written into the customer-data telemetry lake.

assumptions.assumption: The telemetry lake contains confidential data because it contains site addresses and occupancy patterns identified as customer data.
assumptions.basis: The description says the lake has site addresses and occupancy patterns and calls them customer data.

assumptions.assumption: The device registry is in the cloud-services boundary because it is a Firestore registry.
assumptions.basis: The description identifies the device registry as Firestore.

assumptions.assumption: Pub/Sub is in the cloud-services boundary because it is the named cloud messaging service receiving readings.
assumptions.basis: The description identifies Pub/Sub as the service receiving forwarded readings.

assumptions.assumption: The telemetry lake is in the cloud-services boundary because it is in BigQuery.
assumptions.basis: The description identifies the telemetry lake as being in BigQuery.

assumptions.assumption: The Cloud Storage bucket is in the cloud-services boundary because it is a Cloud Storage bucket.
assumptions.basis: The description identifies the firmware location as a Cloud Storage bucket.

assumptions.assumption: The dashboard is in the corporate-network boundary because fleet operators access it from the corporate network.
assumptions.basis: The description says fleet operators look at dashboards from the corporate network.
